passage: Wednesday. Day 6 of the morning plan. Wake at 6:30 no matter what. Curtains open first, the light hits my face and it actually helps. Then ten minutes of stretches, a short walk round the block with Siddharth from next door, and breakfast at the table: idli today. Last week I tried to force bedtime to nine and just stared at the ceiling. This time I'm not fighting the night; I'm fixing the morning and letting the night catch up. Yesterday I fell asleep at 11:20, about forty minutes earlier than usual, without trying. Siddharth says the walk is the best part. I think it's the breakfast. Tomorrow same again, 6:30, curtains, walk, idli or poha. - Madhav

passage:
In Kherwadi village, the school bus left at 7:15, and for months Trisha had missed it twice a week. She'd lie awake till past midnight, then sleep through her mother's calls.

Her older cousin Sunaina, home from nursing college, gave different advice from everyone else. "Don't fight the night. Fix the morning."

So Trisha set a wake time of 6 am, every day, even on the Sunday of the village fair. The first thing she did was step out into the courtyard and throw open the shutters so the early light came in. Then she walked to the well and back with the buffalo, ten minutes. Then a proper breakfast of poha with her grandfather.

The first week, she yawned all day. By the third week, she was tired by ten at night without trying. She hadn't missed the bus in twelve days.

qa.q: What wake time did Trisha set?
qa.a: 6 am, every day, even on the Sunday of the village fair.

qa.q: How did Trisha feel during the first week of the new routine?
qa.a: She felt tired and sleepy all day, probably a little discouraged, before it began to work.

qa.q: What else could Trisha keep in mind as the routine settles?
qa.a: She could keep the wake time steady even after late nights, since the steady morning is what trains her body clock.

qa.q: How might Trisha's mother see the change?
qa.a: Her mother likely feels relieved, no longer calling repeatedly in the mornings while Trisha sleeps through the bus.

grounding: Shows a student setting a fixed wake time with daylight, light exercise and breakfast, since a strong morning routine helps the body clock more than forcing an early bedtime.
